suggestions.title: Log yesterday tonight — it is one of the four days Friday's verdict stands on

rationale.science: Adherence data beats metabolic stories: logging gaps cluster exactly when intake shifts, and an unlogged day inside a test window makes the test unanswerable rather than passed (Alhassan 2008).
rationale.data: Wednesday 8/19 has no food, steps or sleep row. The Friday call — trend at or under 163.8 with the weekdays logged clean — has 8/17 (2,300) and 8/18 (2,081) in, and 8/19 blank.
rationale.relationship: Five fill-in asks in three weeks have each converted inside a day, and every one settled a question the scale alone could not. This one completes the window so tomorrow's read grades the week instead of voiding it. Nothing in the app changes — the act is the log row itself, and rough numbers marked as estimates count.

suggestions.predict: 8/19 lands tonight or tomorrow morning with rough numbers, and Friday's verdict is answerable whichever way it goes.

suggestions.title: Pick the hip thrust's opening load before you leave for the gym — the debut is tomorrow

rationale.science: A debut anchors every later comparison on the lift. Progression guidance wants small planned jumps from a known start (ACSM progression stand); a guessed opener on a new machine spends the first of its four baseline sessions on the guess.
rationale.data: The hip thrust still has no working load and unfilled setup pins, four days after entering the programme. Tomorrow is its debut — on the same session where calves, abs, ham curl, extension and the leg raise all open on fresh baselines.
rationale.relationship: Tomorrow is the most misreadable session in the file: five lifts re-anchoring plus one debut. The load is the only unknown you can remove tonight — the same way the ham 125 check turned that debut into a clean 11,9,9. Enter it in SETUP when you pick it; this card just puts the decision on the record.

suggestions.predict: Load set before the session, and the debut banks a usable baseline in the 8–12 rep window at 1–2 in reserve. If the session runs with it still blank, the first baseline session is spent guessing — the exact cost this card exists to avoid.

suggestions.title: Three machines might be training the short half of the muscle — answer three questions in SETUP

rationale.science: A muscle that crosses two joints grows where the other joint holds it long. Straight-knee calf work grew the gastrocnemius +9–12% against +0.6–1.7% seated in a within-person MRI trial (n=14, untrained — direction more than size); overhead triceps work grew the long head +28.5% vs +19.6% for pushdowns; a seated ham curl trains the hamstrings at length where a lying one does not.
rationale.data: Your SETUP cards do not record which variant each machine is. Calves note a near-straight knee — likely already the right version. The triceps and ham cards read either way, and those two are where the answer is genuinely unknown.
rationale.relationship: On a cut with capped sets, yield per set is the lever — and if any answer comes back the short version, the switch is free and worth more than any rep-mechanics tweak. Nothing changes tonight; the ask is three answers next time you are at the machines.

suggestions.predict: Calves pass. At least one of triceps or ham comes back short-muscle — and if one does, the switch becomes its own card with a fresh-baseline warning attached. If all three pass, this closes for good and machine selection never bothers you again.
